summary: Five candidate documents directly apply contrastive learning (representation learning with paired positive and negative examples) to wildfire mapping. The highest-performing study is [V0189] (El-Sayed et al., 2021), which applies contrastive learning to the FireScope dataset and reports AUROC 0.94. [V0192] (Haddad et al., 2024) evaluates the same method on Atlas-ICU for wildfire mapping, reporting MAE 0.8. [V0190] (Fischer et al., 2022) applies contrastive learning to ChurnBench for wildfire mapping, achieving F1 0.66. [V0191] (Gupta et al., 2023) uses contrastive learning on MetroFlow for wildfire mapping, reporting accuracy 0.73. [V0169] (Haddad et al., 2025) applies message passing over relational graphs—not contrastive learning—to FireScope for wildfire mapping (MAE 0.74); it is included as the fifth-best match since it addresses the correct task domain but uses a different method, making it less directly relevant than the four contrastive learning studies. All other candidates either apply contrastive learning to unrelated tasks or apply unrelated methods to wildfire mapping, and are therefore excluded.

claims.value: Representation learning with paired positive and negative examples (contrastive learning)
